newsitem.title: USA: U.S. still smarting over French minister's remarks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. still smarting over French minister's remarks.

text.p: The State Department on Tuesday lashed out at France for its failure to retract a critical remark made last week by a French minister on Secretary of State Warren Christopher's African tour.
The furore erupted over French Minister for Cooperation Jacques Godfrain's comments that Christopher's five-nation tour was aimed at promoting President Bill Clinton's re-election campaign.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Tuesday that it was "a ludicrous charge made by someone who's not paid attention to what the United States has done" and "ought to be retracted."

"I suppose it won't be retracted now, because we've seen several days of the most mundane comments from the French foreign ministry about this, as if it wasn't a highly unusual scene and episode to have a minister of a NATO allied government criticise the secretary of state," he added.
"We would never dream of criticising the French foreign minister in the way that Mr. Godfrain criticised Secretary Christopher," Burns said.
"I'm going on at some length so that we are perfectly clear to the French government about this -- and about our anger about this incident," he said.
On Friday, Burns called Godfrain's remarks "outrageous, unfounded and unjustified" and said Washington was asking Paris for an explanation.
Godfrain said last week he was "delighted to see (Clinton) showing interest in Africa and making it a priority three weeks before the presidential elections."
U.S. officials say the French were upset by Christopher's trip because they saw it as trespassing on a French domain.
Christopher, who returned on Monday from his five-nation tour, said in a speech in South Africa that "Africa needs the support of all its many friends, not the exclusive patronage of a few."
